title: Had any angel-cult been lawful, Paul would have distinguished it from the abuse
source_text: LXXX. Quod si quis ejusmodi cultus, ex Apostoli sententia Angelis debitus fuisset, si licitum existimavisset festa & Oratoria Angelis consecrare, & in publicis fidelium coetibus hymnos illis canere, eosque invocare, ac coram illis procumbere, non simpliciter damnasset Angelorum culturam, sed siquid immodicum in Angelorum religioso cultu apud Colossenses ab Impostoribus fuisset introductum, illud distincte notavisset, & legitimum Angelorum cultum ab illegitimo quadam ratione secrevisset: ut facerent proculdubio Doctores Scholae Romanae, siqua secta jam exoriretur, quae ipsorum judicio, nimium quid Angelis in hoc genere tribueret.
pass_a_gloss: But if any worship of this kind had, in the Apostle's judgment, been owed to Angels, if he had thought it lawful to consecrate feasts and Oratories to Angels, and in the public assemblies of the faithful to sing hymns to them, and to invoke them, and to fall forward before them, he would not simply have condemned the worship of Angels; but if anything immoderate in the religious worship of Angels had been introduced among the Colossians by Impostors, he would have noted that distinctly, and would in some manner have separated the legitimate worship of Angels from the illegitimate: as the Doctors of the Roman School would without doubt do, if any sect should now arise which, in their judgment, attributed something too much to Angels in this kind.
pass_b_english: If, in the Apostle's judgment, worship of this kind had been owed to angels, and if he had thought it lawful to consecrate feasts and chapels to angels, to sing hymns to them in the public assemblies of the faithful, to invoke them, and to fall down before them, he would not have condemned the worship of angels without qualification.

Had impostors brought some excess into the religious worship of angels among the Colossians, he would have marked it out plainly and would somehow have separated lawful worship of angels from unlawful. That is certainly what the teachers of the Roman school would do if some sect arose now that, in their judgment, gave the angels too much in this respect.

lemmas.latin: nimium quid Angelis in hoc genere tribueret
lemmas.gloss: attributed something too much to angels in this kind

choices.why: Oratories are small places of prayer; 'chapels' is the plain English.
